page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Epipetalous — definition
lines: When the stamens are attached to the petals,
steps.why: Epi = upon, petalous = petals: stamens standing ON the petals instead of free on the thalamus.
common_mistakes: Writing petals attached to stamens - the direction matters: STAMENS are attached to PETALS.
steps.memory_tip: Epi- means upon: stamens upon the petals.
steps.margin_note: One sentence; keep the direction of attachment clear.

steps.label: Example
steps.why: The Solanaceae flowers are the standard examples - the book's example line is cut off as 'Datu'; the intended plant is Datura.
common_mistakes: Giving lily as the example. In lily the stamens sit on the tepals - that condition is epiphyllous.
steps.memory_tip: Datura and brinjal - one family (Solanaceae), both epipetalous.
steps.margin_note: One correct plant name is the full mark.
